title: Memphis Mayor Paul Young issues executive order for data center action
source_used: Memphis Flyer (The Commercial Appeal is blocked, HTTP 402); Daily Memphian confirms headline
key_facts: On Friday (9 Oct 2026) Memphis Mayor Paul Young issued an executive order declaring a 90-day policy review to help the city formulate data centre protocols.
The study covers land use and neighbourhood protections, infrastructure, air quality, water and aquifer protections, energy and utility costs, and noise.
Young will appoint experts; they will write a report with recommendations and potential guardrails for the mayor within 90 days and present it publicly.
The order requires at least three community education sessions and a public comment period.
The recommendations would go to bodies including the City Council, the Shelby County Health Department and Memphis Light, Gas and Water.
Young said the order 'does not suspend, delay, restrict, or interfere with council action'; the study runs alongside the council's consideration of data centre ordinances, including a moratorium.
The council voted 7-5 on Tuesday to hold off voting on several ordinances until 20 Oct; the council attorney warned of legal limits on a moratorium.
quote_evidence: "The study will proceed concurrently with the Memphis City Council's ongoing consideration of data center legislation," Young said.
"The executive order does not suspend, delay, restrict, or interfere with council action."
why_it_matters_hint: The mayor starts an expert study of data centre rules while the council's vote on a pause is delayed to 20 Oct.
notes: Commercial Appeal original blocked (HTTP 402); Memphis Flyer wrote its own report; the Daily Memphian headline confirms the order and a 90-day working group.
